# USGS Water agent operations and customer receiving

The maintained merchant MCP now opens the original USGS Water project and operator console. An analyst and an agent work with the same project revision, retained provider captures, source reviews, immutable editions, HEC-DSS plans, native exports and original job state. The customer command downloads a complete source/native handover and receives it through that same Water project engine.

The native scientific mapping, format, time and quality rules remain documented in [DSS.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usgs-water/DSS.md). This guide covers the complete agent and customer workflow. The existing [Water operator guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usgs-water/README.md) covers the source console and original merchant/buyer operations.

## 1. Attach original projects

Create a private connection file. Declare each original project once under a stable lower-case alias. Project directories must already exist at their canonical paths with mode 0700. Connection and selected mapping/handover files are private regular files with mode 0600.

    {
      "schema": "stellar-forge.usgs-workspace-connection.v1",
      "workspaces": {
        "potomac": {
          "label": "Potomac daily flow",
          "directory": "/private/water-project",
          "files": {
            "mapping": {
              "kind": "mapping",
              "path": "/private/potomac-mapping.json",
              "sha256": "<complete mapping-file SHA256>"
            }
          }
        },
        "received": {
          "label": "Received analyst project",
          "directory": "/private/received-water",
          "files": {}
        }
      }
    }

Relative paths in this file resolve against its directory. There may be 1–32 workspace aliases and up to 128 selected file handles per alias. A handle's kind is mapping or handover; its optional configured SHA256 pins the operator's original selection. MCP arguments select these aliases and handles. Executable paths and arbitrary host paths are host configuration.

From repository source:

    node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/serve.mjs init-usgs-workspaces \
      --dir /private/water-mcp \
      --connection /private/water-connection.json

    node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/serve.mjs serve \
      --config /private/water-mcp/merchant-mcp.json \
      --port 3211 --token-env MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN

Use the existing host bearer secret in MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN. It must be printable ASCII and at least 24 characters. The maintained server also retains its existing OAuth hosting options. An original general merchant initialization can attach this connection with --usgs-workspaces; an existing merchant configuration can set usgsWorkspaceConnection to this private file.

The portable product exposes these same commands as merchant-mcp and merchant-usgs. It includes the original source dependencies and this guide. The customer operations are also available as:

    node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/serve.mjs usgs --help

Native DSS creation, readback and runtime inspection use the official interpreter configured on the host through USGS_HECDSS_PYTHON. Use the original DSS runtime guide to install or select it. The MCP caller does not choose a Python executable.

## 2. Open and inspect the shared project

Call merchant_usgs_workspaces to inspect the declared aliases and selected file handles. Then open the original project:

    {"workspace":"potomac"}

Pass that object to merchant_usgs_open. Its returned URL opens the original Water console. A second open through this host reuses that console. Close/reopen retains the same project files and native operation identities.

Use merchant_usgs_status for current project revision, original job progress, counts and active retained reads. merchant_usgs_inventory pages captures, reviews, editions, dssExports, jobs or history. For example:

    {"workspace":"potomac","kind":"captures","limit":25}

Each page contains total, snapshot, offset, items and nextOffset. Follow nextOffset with the same expectedSnapshot. A changed original collection reports USGS_INVENTORY_CHANGED so the caller can inspect page zero again. Pages honor both the requested row limit and the encoded response size. The returned nextOffset is authoritative.

Save an explicit source selection with merchant_usgs_project_save, including title, selection and the current expectedRevision. Start or resume a capture with merchant_usgs_capture_start and its stable captureId and expectedRevision. The original console retains provider pages and job progress. merchant_usgs_capture_cancel reaches the same original acquisition.

After an interrupted source call, inspect the original capture ID and retained pages before resuming it. The source IDs and provider observations remain attached to the original project revision. Acquisition is an explicit operation; opening, inspection, file retrieval and customer receiving do not reacquire USGS data.

## 3. Analyze, compare and retain the decision

merchant_usgs_capture returns source metadata and page count. merchant_usgs_capture_pages returns original response URLs, exact hashes and retrieval metadata. merchant_usgs_capture_file_read retrieves a selected page by its original pageIndex.

Run merchant_usgs_analysis with captureId, optional original comparisonCaptureId and the original analysis options. The default series view returns series identities, exact summary statistics and counts. It does not expand every time observation inside each series.

The view parameter supports these complete source-preserving reads:

| View | Original data returned | Additional selection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| series | Series identities, current/baseline summaries and counts | None |
| source-pages | Exact pages that belong to the analysis | None |
| observations | Original current-window time observations | seriesKey |
| baseline-observations | Original baseline-window time observations | seriesKey |
| conflicts | Conflicting feature identities and retained version counts | None |
| conflict-records | Complete retained versions of one conflicting feature | featureKey |
| added, removed, changed | Corresponding original capture comparison records | comparisonCaptureId when analyzing |
| unresolved | Original unresolved comparison identities and side counts | comparisonCaptureId when analyzing |
| unresolved-previous, unresolved-current | Complete records for one side of an unresolved feature | featureKey |

For example, obtain a series key from the default result and then request:

    {
      "workspace": "potomac",
      "captureId": "usgs-october-01-07",
      "view": "observations",
      "seriesKey": "<complete original series key>",
      "limit": 100
    }

All these collections use the same snapshot/offset contract. Comparison views require an actual original comparison capture; an absent comparison is not reported as zero changes.

Retain a decision with merchant_usgs_review_save using reviewId, captureId, the reviewed expectedCaptureSha256, the same options/comparison and a note. The original immutable review binds the analysis, source and decision. Repeat the same ID and inputs to reopen it after a lost reply. A different decision under that ID is rejected.

merchant_usgs_review applies the same views to the saved review. For large analyses, retain the review once and page it instead of repeatedly recomputing the original analysis. merchant_usgs_review_file_read provides the complete native JSON, HTML, CSV or GeoJSON export. Unusually large individual records remain available through those original file exports or the exact source page.

Prepare the original source edition with merchant_usgs_edition_prepare using the existing reviewId and a stable editionId. merchant_usgs_edition pages its original member manifest. merchant_usgs_edition_file_read selects an exact member from that manifest and preserves its byte hash.

## 4. Review and run the native DSS mapping

Use merchant_usgs_dss_source with the retained editionId. This exposes original source identity and paged series, including units, observation states, clock information and approval counts.

A mapping is the complete native starforge.usgs-dss-mapping.v1 object described by DSS.md. Pass it inline to merchant_usgs_dss_preview, or select the declared mappingFile and expectedMappingFileSha256. To inspect a configured handle first:

    {"workspace":"potomac","file":"mapping"}

Use merchant_usgs_configured_file. The preview using that handle is:

    {
      "workspace": "potomac",
      "editionId": "october-water",
      "mappingFile": "mapping",
      "expectedMappingFileSha256": "<reviewed complete mapping-file SHA256>"
    }

The preview returns the original planSha256, source identity, native totals and series settings. Every selected series keeps its original key. The complete mapping explicitly identifies excluded series. A previousDssId selects the retained original comparison export and source.

Start with merchant_usgs_dss_start using the same edition/mapping selection, a stable dssId and that exact expectedPlanSha256. This starts the original console job and original native writer. It does not introduce another job engine.

Inspect merchant_usgs_dss_operation and the original jobs inventory. An unchanged completed DSS ID reopens its original result without another native write. An interrupted operation retains its plan and operation identity for inspection. The complete original plan is available through merchant_usgs_dss_file_read with kind=plan, including before native completion.

Native inspection and delivery kinds are dss, report, mapping, rows, native, comparison, plan and handover. The plan and mapping files preserve complete per-series selections and excluded observations, while the default MCP response supplies compact native summaries. A source or file hash change is reported against the exact retained selection.

Use merchant_usgs_dss_runtime to inspect the original host runtime. merchant_usgs_dss_verify starts the original native readback job against the saved DSS and mapped request. Readback is a separate explicit operation and retains its native comparison result.

## 5. Prepare a complete customer delivery

First call merchant_usgs_dss_handover on the completed native export. It starts or reopens the original complete handover job. Inspect the original job and then merchant_usgs_dss_file with kind=handover.

Once that original ZIP is retained, create a stable customer delivery:

    {
      "workspace": "potomac",
      "dssId": "potomac-daily-20261012-7737",
      "exportId": "potomac-dss"
    }

Pass this object to merchant_usgs_delivery_prepare. The customer exportId is a lower-case alias of up to 64 characters. It is distinct from the original native DSS ID, which retains the original Water naming rules.

The compact usgs-delivery.json completion manifest binds the customer ID, configured workspace, original native DSS ID, native export hash, plan hash, source identity, totals and complete handover ZIP's exact name/bytes/SHA256. Retaining this manifest does not copy or rebuild the original handover.

The manifest is published as a complete single-link file under the original Linux state lease. A process interruption leaves either the existing complete manifest or a resumable uncommitted temporary file. Repeating an identical delivery ID returns the same manifest. Reusing it for a different source or handover reports USGS_DELIVERY_CONFLICT.

merchant_usgs_deliveries finds retained deliveries after restart or a lost prepare reply. merchant_usgs_delivery_manifest supplies the manifest file's exact hash. Customer file reads work from the retained original project after host restart without opening its console or running another DSS job.

This transfer is authenticated operator delivery. Original Water edition sales use the existing stage, merchant, buy-prepare, buy and buy-reopen commands with their original payment configuration and buyer intent IDs.

## 6. Download, interrupt and resume

Inspect the exact delivery from the maintained CLI:

    merchant-usgs inspect --url http://127.0.0.1:3211/mcp \
      --export-id potomac-dss

Retain the returned manifestSha256, then download:

    merchant-usgs download --url http://127.0.0.1:3211/mcp \
      --export-id potomac-dss \
      --manifest-sha <reviewed-manifest-SHA256> \
      --out /private/potomac-download

Use an HTTPS endpoint for a remote host or the original loopback HTTP listener. The bearer comes from MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN or --token-env. Credentials stay in the caller's environment.

The downloader is the maintained retained-download.mjs transport. It keeps its original Linux flock lease, original completion manifest and durable byte checkpoint. Each completed chunk is flushed before the checkpoint advances. Ctrl-C, a lost transport response or a host restart can be recovered by repeating the same command and directory.

A resumed download checks the retained prefix, reacquires an expired read at the same exact file/hash/offset, and preserves completed files. Only an owned uncheckpointed suffix can be discarded. A different endpoint, manifest, file hash or unrelated directory content is rejected instead of overwriting the original download.

Chunks are up to 196608 bytes. --chunk-bytes selects a smaller positive chunk size. The first read of an original large descriptor may need to hash the complete file; that call has a 30-minute timeout while subsequent reads use the ordinary request timeout. The caller's cancellation signal remains active throughout.

The server's shared reader streams and verifies the original native file descriptor. It does not buffer a complete multi-GiB handover or create a second whole-file snapshot. Native DSS member files retain their original size limits; complete handovers may be up to 8 GiB. Four live reads share this provider's retained-read limit. EOF, release, expiry and provider shutdown release the original descriptors.

## 7. Receive and reopen the complete project

Receive a completed download into an original private Water project outside the download directory:

    merchant-usgs receive \
      --dir /private/potomac-download \
      --project /private/received-water \
      --export-id potomac-dss \
      --manifest-sha <reviewed-manifest-SHA256>

The receiver checks the completed local checkpoint and manifest, streams the exact selected ZIP, verifies its complete byte hash before EOF, and passes the expected native export, source and plan identities to the original Water receiver. That original receiver validates its staged edition/export manifests before either destination is installed.

A wrong selected identity leaves the existing destination editions and exports unchanged. A matching package installs the original source edition and original native DSS export. Repeating the same package reopens those IDs. The original receiver handles a previously interrupted matching installation without creating another source edition or DSS export.

Add --verify to run the original native HEC-DSS readback on the receiving host. This requires its configured official interpreter and native library. Receiving does not execute code from the downloaded archive.

Open the received original console:

    merchant-usgs serve --project /private/received-water --port 0

The CLI prints its original loopback URL. Ctrl-C closes the original console and its owned resources.

Agents can also receive through merchant_usgs_dss_receive into an open declared workspace. Select either a declared handover file handle or fromWorkspace plus the original dssId, and provide the exact expectedSha256. The same native receiving engine performs the installation.

## 8. File and lifecycle contracts

For ordinary source, review, edition and DSS file tools, the first read returns a readId and exact file metadata. Continue with that readId, expectedSha256, offset and limit. Use nextOffset from the reply. A final null nextOffset releases the descriptor. merchant_usgs_file_release explicitly closes an unfinished workspace read.

Customer delivery file tools additionally bind exportId and expectedManifestSha256. The maintained downloader handles this protocol, file release and host-restart continuation.

merchant_usgs_close advances the workspace's admission generation, aborts in-flight native requests, cancels the original project jobs, drains previously admitted calls and closes its file scope. Old setup continuations cannot attach after that close. A subsequent open can use the same retained project again.

The full merchant provider begins USGS cancellation before waiting for its admitted mutation. Close and capture-cancel remain reachable while a long receive is admitted. Only this host's owned console/jobs/readers are stopped. Independent customer delivery reads retain their separate delivery scopes until EOF, explicit release, idle expiry or provider shutdown.

## Programmatic use

The distribution exports:

- ./merchant/mcp/usgs-workspaces: MerchantUSGSWorkspaces, connection reader and the 35 tool definitions.
- ./merchant/mcp/usgs-delivery: the original delivery schema, parser and handover limit.
- ./merchant/mcp/usgs-download: inspectUSGSCustomer, downloadUSGSCustomer and receiveUSGSCustomer.
- ./seller/usgs-water/dss: original scientific planning, native export and staged receiving.

The customer functions accept the same endpoint, token environment, manifest and directory selections as the CLI. downloadUSGSCustomer also accepts signal, chunkSize and onProgress. receiveUSGSCustomer takes the reviewed expectedManifestSha256 and an explicit optional verify flag. Completion returns the retained original IDs and a command for reopening the original Water console.

# Ruby and Rails customer applications

A seller can deliver its current OpenAPI contract as a complete Ruby customer package. The application constructs the selected request with the generated seller implementation, prepares it through the installed Node Buyer, reviews its exact terms and body, executes through the existing operator, and receives a complete response that can be reopened offline.

The package also includes a durable receiving service for Rails jobs. A stable business key selects one native intent. The application can restart, recover the same operation, import its complete saved response, and resume database processing without requesting another purchase.

## Create and deliver the customer package

Use the current seller OpenAPI exported by the maintained merchant workspace:

~~~sh
starforge client ruby export --openapi /absolute/seller-openapi.json --out /absolute/customer-package
starforge client ruby status --dir /absolute/customer-package
~~~

The same command is available directly from this source:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/developer/ruby-client/export.mjs \
  export --openapi /absolute/seller-openapi.json --out /absolute/customer-package
~~~

An already completed JavaScript customer export can receive its Ruby companions with:

~~~sh
starforge client ruby resume --dir /absolute/existing-customer-export
~~~

The exporter preserves the original five JavaScript files and their existing client-export.json. It adds eight Ruby application files and writes ruby-client.json after every companion is complete. Each file carries an exact byte count and SHA-256. The Ruby manifest also binds the original client-export.json and seller source hash.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| seller_client.rb | Ruby request, Buyer, Operation and offline Delivery APIs |
| seller_client.rbs | Generated operation-ID types and public API signatures |
| seller-client-bridge.mjs | Finite request construction through the generated buildRequest |
| seller-buyer-bridge.mjs | Original Node Buyer preparation, review, execution, recovery and saved-file receiving |
| seller-contract.json | Complete selected source and operation descriptions |
| rails_receiving.rb | Stable business-job preparation, explicit execution and receiving |
| customer.rb | Runnable customer CLI and one repeatable operator journey |
| RUBY.md | This operating and Rails integration guide |

Use exact-copy delivery when transferring an existing package:

~~~sh
starforge client ruby copy --dir /absolute/customer-package --out /absolute/recipient-package
starforge client ruby copy-resume --dir /absolute/customer-package --out /absolute/interrupted-recipient
~~~

Copy and copy-resume retain the selected bytes and original manifests. Additive resume completes an interrupted export from the matching source; a conflicting companion file requires its existing source version or a new destination. Keep the completed package with the customer application so a later seller deployment does not change an existing job's contract.

## Runtime and host selection

Use Linux, Ruby 3.1 or newer with JSON, BigDecimal, CSV and the other standard libraries used by seller_client.rb, and the installed Node 24 SF88 buyer runtime. Preparation and execution load that runtime's node/index.mjs and CLI from the host-selected directory. The customer package contains application adapters; the native operator, signing integration, policy, wallet, HTTP transport, reconciliation and ledger come from that existing installation.

Each application selects a private buyer state directory. The same state directory and intent reopen the same operation. Select either an existing operator profile or an initialized native buyer workspace. The workspace route preserves its own configuration and operator identity.

~~~ruby
require_relative "customer-package/rails_receiving"

client = Starforge::SellerClient.new("/absolute/customer-package")
buyer = Starforge::Buyer.new(
  client: client,
  runtime_directory: "/absolute/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli",
  state_directory: "/absolute/private/ruby-buyer",
  workspace_directory: "/absolute/private/original-buyer-workspace"
)
~~~

For a profile-based customer, replace workspace_directory with operator_profile pointing to the original private profile JSON. Host environment variables remain available to the original signing and approval integrations. The adapter removes Node runtime injection variables NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH. It preserves the host's original stdin and existing approval-broker environment for the native operator; approval continues in that original terminal or browser session.

Call buyer.close during application or worker shutdown. It closes admission, cancels active child calls, and waits for their cleanup. Request generation uses a finite JSON input; payment and receiving calls use private files and the original Node child lifecycle. Each call has a timeout, a private process result, and a durable response. A process cancellation leaves the original buyer's recorded attempt available for recovery.

## Select a real operation and retain its request

Inspect the delivered contract before selecting an operation:

~~~sh
ruby /absolute/customer-package/customer.rb contract --package /absolute/customer-package
~~~

In Ruby, client.operations returns the exact operation descriptions and payment choices. Select the actual operation ID, path/query inputs, payment alternative and atomic ceiling from that contract.

~~~ruby
key = "monthly-source-refresh:account-42:2026-10"
bound = client.build_request(
  ENV.fetch("SELLER_OPERATION_ID"),
  {
    "path" => JSON.parse(File.read("/absolute/private/path-inputs.json")),
    "query" => JSON.parse(File.read("/absolute/private/query-inputs.json"))
  },
  intent_id: Starforge::Receiving.intent_id(key),
  max_atomic: ENV.fetch("SELECTED_MAX_ATOMIC"),
  accept_index: Integer(ENV.fetch("SELECTED_ACCEPT_INDEX"))
)
bound.save("/absolute/private/retained-request")
~~~

Require rails_receiving.rb before using Receiving.intent_id. A plain Ruby application can instead choose its own stable intent string and use seller_client.rb directly.

build_request delegates serialization and original offer matching to the delivered JavaScript buildRequest. Ruby inputs use string keys. Path and query values follow that operation's original schema, including repeated query values. Payment ceilings remain decimal strings, including values above JavaScript's exact integer range. Integer JSON request values outside that range are rejected; use an exact string when the actual seller schema specifies a string. Unsupported Ruby objects, cycles, duplicate JSON keys and nonfinite numbers are rejected before the request bridge runs.

Use inputs["body"] for a JSON request. For an optional body, inputs["omitBody"] follows the original generator. For multipart requests, supply the complete existing multipart body as a binary Ruby String and its exact Content-Type:

~~~ruby
inputs = {
  "multipart" => {
    "body" => File.binread("/absolute/private/request.multipart"),
    "contentType" => File.read("/absolute/private/request.content-type").strip
  }
}
~~~

The adapter does not rebuild multipart boundaries. It binds the resulting body length and digest to the original request. The bridge accepts bodies up to 16 MiB and envelopes up to 64 MiB. The original generated runtime also enforces its existing JSON-body and operation-specific limits.

BoundRequest.save retains request-input.json, the generated request.json, optional request.body and request-plan.json. client.load_request verifies those bytes and reconstructs the same request using the retained customer package. The manifest and source hashes travel into the original operation's ruby-seller-source.json.

## Prepare, review, execute and recover

The direct API exposes the existing original buyer operation:

~~~ruby
begin
  operation = client.prepare(buyer, bound)
  review = operation.review
  # Present and inspect this actual native review in the existing operator flow.
  result = operation.execute(review: review)
  puts result.fetch("status")
ensure
  buyer.close
end
~~~

execute requires the selected review. The native operator still performs its own approval and policy checks. Keep this call in the actual operator session, with its original terminal or scoped browser approval integration. Background receiving jobs use recover and receive.

Operation.status returns its native state, delivery status, retry guidance and bound seller source. Operation.recover reads the same saved result and original native output. It returns nil when that operation has no recoverable result. A recoverable transport result preserves the native status, exit information, runtime error, response descriptor and stream metadata.

Each application call has a UUID separate from the purchase intent. Pass call_id when the application already retains a transport request ID. Repeating that UUID returns its saved response or reports the original unavailable reply. It does not blindly repeat a dispatched child. The original buyer's create-only attempt record independently preserves the same purchase across Ruby and Node restarts.

A new call ID is appropriate for a fresh read of evolving status or recovery. Repeating a preparation with the same exact bound request adopts an existing matching prepared operation. Repeating an execution still reaches the original single-attempt protection. Preserve an incomplete native preparation and its original state if the native runtime reports that it needs recovery.

## Receive complete data and reopen offline

After the original result contains a SAVED response, receive it into a private directory:

~~~ruby
operation = client.reopen(buyer, bound.intent_id)
delivery = operation.receive("/absolute/private/customer-receipt")
expected_manifest = delivery.manifest_sha256
~~~

Receiving copies the saved response through the existing Node result.verify and result.saveAs implementation. It retains the selected source, request, body when present, review, native result and complete response.bin. A saved receiving plan binds those files before copying, so interrupted recovery uses the same selected result. customer-delivery.json completes the handoff.

The response's native status remains in result.json. A saved response may be an application error response; inspect its original status and runtime information before applying business changes.

A later process can reopen without Node or network:

~~~ruby
require_relative "customer-package/seller_client"

delivery = Starforge::Delivery.open(
  "/absolute/private/customer-receipt",
  expected_manifest_sha256: expected_manifest
)
data = delivery.json
~~~

Delivery.open verifies every complete file, the selected manifest and source/request/review/result bindings. Each data reader uses a complete private snapshot whose SHA-256 is checked before application code receives bytes. This keeps database callbacks from acting on a response that fails its final digest.

Use delivery.bytes for a bounded binary response, each_chunk for streaming, json for JSON, and each_csv for CSV. JSON response integers retain Ruby precision and decimal values use BigDecimal. CSV with headers returns CSV::Row, retaining duplicate column names and their original order. Select fields according to the actual delivered schema.

~~~ruby
delivery.each_csv do |row|
  original_fields = row.fields
  original_headers = row.headers
  # Apply the project's explicit field mapping here.
end
~~~

Receiving artifacts are private application data. Preserve the expected manifest hash in the application's job/database record when transferring a handoff to another machine.

## One complete customer command

Create a private settings JSON using the actual installed runtime and existing host workspace:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.ruby-customer-settings.v1",
  "runtimeDirectory": "/absolute/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli",
  "buyerDirectory": "/absolute/private/ruby-buyer",
  "jobsDirectory": "/absolute/private/customer-jobs",
  "workspaceDirectory": "/absolute/private/original-buyer-workspace",
  "node": "/absolute/bin/node",
  "timeout": 420,
  "responseFile": {
    "maxBytes": 67108864,
    "timeoutMs": 30000
  }
}
~~~

The request JSON contains operationId, inputs, maxAtomic, and optional acceptIndex/paymentFlow. Use actual values from seller-contract.json. For this CLI's multipart input, supply inputs.multipart.bodyBase64 and contentType; the CLI decodes the complete original bytes before calling the Ruby API.

~~~sh
ruby /absolute/customer-package/customer.rb run \
  --package /absolute/customer-package \
  --settings /absolute/private/customer-settings.json \
  --request /absolute/private/selected-request.json \
  --key monthly-source-refresh-account-42-2026-10
~~~

This prepares the original operation, retains its review and recovers any existing result. Add --execute in the original operator session to continue the explicit native execution. Once a response is saved, the same command receives and verifies the complete handoff.

Subsequent calls can omit --request to load the retained request plan. prepare, review, execute, recover, receive and status are also individual commands with the same settings and key. The first settings bytes are retained beside the job and must match on later calls.

A completed repeat reopens the original receiving result offline. The explicit offline command needs only the jobs root, stable key and optional expected manifest:

~~~sh
ruby /absolute/customer-package/customer.rb reopen \
  --jobs-directory /absolute/private/customer-jobs \
  --key monthly-source-refresh-account-42-2026-10 \
  --manifest-sha256 ORIGINAL_CUSTOMER_DELIVERY_SHA256
~~~

The original customer-result.json records source/package/manifest identity, native status and exact delivered files. Its state RECEIVED describes completed receiving. Keep its native status when presenting the result to users.

## Rails service and Active Job integration

rails_receiving.rb is framework independent. It can be called from a Rails service, job or console without adding a second queue. The business key should come from a persisted model identity and edition, such as a source-import row's UUID. Keep that key unchanged across framework retries.

~~~ruby
require Rails.root.join("vendor", "seller-package", "rails_receiving").to_s

class SellerImport
  def self.open(import)
    client = Starforge::SellerClient.new(import.package_directory)
    buyer = Starforge::Buyer.new(
      client: client,
      runtime_directory: import.runtime_directory,
      state_directory: import.buyer_directory,
      workspace_directory: import.original_workspace_directory
    )
    bound = client.load_request(import.request_directory)
    service = Starforge::Receiving.new(
      client: client,
      buyer: buyer,
      directory: import.jobs_directory,
      key: import.business_key,
      bound: bound,
      response_file: import.response_options
    )
    yield service
  ensure
    buyer&.close
  end
end
~~~

The fields in this service belong to your existing model. Store the actual selected host, package and request paths at import creation. Build and save that request with Receiving.intent_id(import.business_key), so the service can bind it to the same job.

An operator prepares and reviews the source import, then executes through the existing native operator session. The service retains one execution UUID before dispatch and verifies the saved review on repeat. A lost response is recovered from the original buyer.

~~~ruby
SellerImport.open(import) do |service|
  review = service.review
  # Existing operator UI/terminal presents this review.
  service.execute(review: review)
end
ReceiveSellerImportJob.perform_later(import.id)
~~~

The job receives and applies the resulting data. The example below illustrates one transaction and a retained manifest check; use your project's actual schema and uniqueness key.

~~~ruby
class ReceiveSellerImportJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :source_imports

  def perform(import_id)
    import = SourceImport.find(import_id)
    delivery = nil
    SellerImport.open(import) { |service| delivery = service.receive }
    payload = delivery.json

    import.with_lock do
      if import.received_manifest_sha256.present?
        raise "Different source receipt" unless
          import.received_manifest_sha256 == delivery.manifest_sha256
        return
      end
      SourceImport.transaction do
        # The existing domain service validates the real payload and uses its
        # actual unique source identifiers for inserts/updates.
        SourceImportApplier.call(import, payload)
        import.update!(
          received_manifest_sha256: delivery.manifest_sha256,
          received_directory: delivery.directory,
          received_at: Time.current
        )
      end
    end
  end
end
~~~

The domain apply and receipt update occur in the same database transaction. A retry after commit finds the original manifest and returns. A retry before commit reuses the same saved response. File receiving is complete before that transaction starts, keeping network/process lifetime outside the database lock.

Classify service errors in the existing application queue. An unfinished original response can be reviewed or recovered; changed source/request/receipt identities require resolving that original selection. Ordinary framework retry configuration applies to receiving and domain writes. Rails documents retry_on, discard_on and transaction behavior in its [Active Job guide](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_job_basics.html).

## Source and operations reference

The generated seller implementation and installed original Node Buyer remain the authority for supported operation inputs, payment options, approval, execution and recovery:

- [Seller developer interface](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/main/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/DEVELOPER.md)
- [Original Node buyer](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/main/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/node/README.md)
- [Ruby process and pipe interfaces](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/3.3/Open3.html)
- [Ruby JSON implementation](https://github.com/ruby/json/blob/master/lib/json/common.rb)
- [Rails Active Job](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_job_basics.html)

Package inspection and copy read complete source bytes. The customer program supplies the practical operator journey over the actual selected merchant request and host. Preserve its result and native workspace with the delivered edition when handing operation to the next maintainer.

The customer command retains `customer-request.json` before native preparation or execution. Supplying `--request` again with a completed job checks the original operation, input values and atomic limit in Ruby; omitting it reopens the retained selection. Offline receiving also binds the delivery manifest to the original business intent and seller source.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""MIT. Compare complete projections made by the retained original XLSX reader.
The parent holds descriptors 3/4 (originals), 5 (difference JSONL), 6 (reader).
SQLite and projection files are private temporary join material, never a source store.
"""
import csv
import gc
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
import tempfile

NATIVE = {}
LIMIT = 256 * 1024 * 1024

def encoded(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False,
                      separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")

def fail(code, message, details=None):
    NATIVE["fail"](code, message, details)

def scalar_token(value, spec):
    if value == "" and spec["nullable"]:
        return ["null", ""]
    kind = spec["type"]
    if kind == "number":
        number = float(value)
        return [kind, "0" if number == 0 else number.hex()]
    if kind == "integer":
        return [kind, str(int(value))]
    return [kind, value]

def headers(fd, descriptor):
    with os.fdopen(os.dup(fd), "rb") as source:
        source.seek(0)
        workbook = NATIVE["Workbook"](source, descriptor["source"])
        try:
            plan = descriptor["plan"]
            bounds = NATIVE["selection_range"](plan["range"])
            left, top, right, bottom = bounds
            header_row = plan.get("headerRow")
            if header_row is not None:
                NATIVE["integer"](header_row, "Header row", top, bottom)
            sheet = workbook.sheet(plan["sheet"])
            values = []
            for col in range(left, right + 1):
                cell = sheet["cells"].get((col, header_row)) if header_row is not None else None
                values.append({"source": NATIVE["column_label"](col),
                               "header": cell.get("value") if cell else None,
                               "cell": cell})
            return {"sheet": plan["sheet"], "range": NATIVE["range_name"](bounds),
                    "headerRow": header_row, "headers": values,
                    "metadata": sheet["metadata"], "epoch": workbook.epoch}
        finally:
            workbook.zip.close()
            workbook.cache.clear()

def project(db, table, fd, descriptor, keys, directory):
    schema = NATIVE["schema_columns"](descriptor["config"])
    specs = {item["name"]: item for item in schema}
    with os.fdopen(os.dup(fd), "rb") as source:
        source.seek(0)
        workbook = NATIVE["Workbook"](source, descriptor["source"])
        try:
            csv_path = os.path.join(directory, table + ".csv")
            map_path = os.path.join(directory, table + ".jsonl")
            with open(csv_path, "x+b") as csv_file, open(map_path, "x+b") as row_file:
                os.chmod(csv_path, 0o600)
                os.chmod(map_path, 0o600)
                config = descriptor["config"]
                projection = NATIVE["prepare"](workbook, {
                    "plan": descriptor["plan"], "config": config,
                    "maxCsvBytes": config.get("maxBytes", 64 * 1024 * 1024),
                    "maxPreparedBytes": min(LIMIT, config.get("maxBytes", 64 * 1024 * 1024) + 64 * 1024 * 1024)
                }, csv_file, row_file)
                csv_file.flush()
                row_file.flush()
                csv_file.seek(0)
                row_file.seek(0)
                sheet = workbook.sheet(descriptor["plan"]["sheet"])
                cols = [(item["name"], NATIVE["column_number"](item["sourceColumn"]))
                        for item in projection["columns"]]
                csv_text = io.TextIOWrapper(csv_file, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
                rows_text = io.TextIOWrapper(row_file, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
                try:
                    records = csv.reader(csv_text)
                    header = next(records)
                    if header != [item["name"] for item in schema]:
                        fail("WORKBOOK_PROJECTION_CHANGED", "The original projection headers changed.")
                    observation = hashlib.sha256()
                    count = 0
                    for values, row_line in zip(records, rows_text, strict=True):
                        row_map = json.loads(row_line)
                        if row_map["record"] != count or len(values) != len(header):
                            fail("WORKBOOK_PROJECTION_CHANGED", "The original source-row map is inconsistent.")
                        row_number = row_map["row"]
                        projected = dict(zip(header, values))
                        tokens = {name: scalar_token(projected[name], specs[name]) for name in header}
                        key_values = [tokens[name] for name in keys]
                        if any(item[0] == "null" for item in key_values):
                            fail("WORKBOOK_NULL_ROW_KEY",
                                 "Choose row keys populated in every selected record.",
                                 {"side": table, "sheet": projection["sheet"], "row": row_number, "keys": keys})
                        key = encoded(key_values).decode("utf-8")
                        cells = {name: sheet["cells"].get((col, row_number),
                                 NATIVE["blank_cell"](col, row_number, row_number in sheet["hidden"]))
                                 for name, col in cols}
                        record = {"row": row_number,
                                  "values": {name: None if tokens[name][0] == "null" else projected[name]
                                             for name in header},
                                  "cells": cells}
                        record_json = encoded(record).decode("utf-8")
                        try:
                            db.execute("INSERT INTO " + table + " VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                                       (key, row_number, record_json, encoded(tokens).decode("utf-8")))
                        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
                            previous = db.execute("SELECT row_number FROM " + table + " WHERE key=?", (key,)).fetchone()
                            fail("WORKBOOK_DUPLICATE_ROW_KEY",
                                 "Choose a unique key or composite key before comparing these editions.",
                                 {"side": table, "sheet": projection["sheet"], "firstRow": previous[0],
                                  "row": row_number, "keys": keys,
                                  "key": [{"type": specs[name]["type"], "text": projected[name]} for name in keys]})
                        observation.update(encoded(record))
                        observation.update(b"\n")
                        count += 1
                    if count != projection["rowCount"]:
                        fail("WORKBOOK_PROJECTION_CHANGED", "The complete projection row count changed.")
                    projection["observationSha256"] = observation.hexdigest()
                    projection["valueBasis"] = "original-reader CSV tokens and original-loader scalar coercion"
                    return projection
                finally:
                    csv_text.detach()
                    rows_text.detach()
        finally:
            workbook.zip.close()
            workbook.cache.clear()

def cell_value(cell):
    if cell is None:
        return None
    # Coordinates are represented independently as row/column movement. Style
    # table IDs can change between packages without changing the number format.
    value = {key: cell.get(key) for key in ("type", "value", "raw", "present",
             "formula", "cachedPresent", "numberFormat", "dateStyle", "hiddenRow")}
    # Shared-string indexes describe package storage, not a changed literal.
    # Keep the exact index in the original cell record but compare its text.
    if value["type"] == "string":
        value["raw"] = value["value"]
    return value

def compare(request):
    baseline_schema = NATIVE["schema_columns"](request["baseline"]["config"])
    target_schema = NATIVE["schema_columns"](request["target"]["config"])
    before_specs = {x["name"]: x for x in baseline_schema}
    after_specs = {x["name"]: x for x in target_schema}
    keys = request.get("keys")
    if not isinstance(keys, list) or not 1 <= len(keys) <= 16 or any(not isinstance(x, str) for x in keys) or len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
        fail("WORKBOOK_ROW_KEYS_REQUIRED", "Choose 1–16 distinct declared public fields as row keys.")
    for name in keys:
        if name not in before_specs or name not in after_specs or before_specs[name]["type"] != after_specs[name]["type"]:
            fail("WORKBOOK_ROW_KEY_SCHEMA_CHANGED",
                 "Each row key must exist with the same original public type in both editions.", {"field": name})
    maximum = request.get("maxReportBytes", 128 * 1024 * 1024)
    if type(maximum) is not int or not 1 <= maximum <= LIMIT:
        fail("WORKBOOK_COMPARISON_CAPACITY", "Choose a comparison report limit within 256 MiB.")
    fields = list(before_specs) + [x for x in after_specs if x not in before_specs]
    counts = {kind: 0 for kind in ("added", "removed", "changed", "source", "moved", "unchanged", "ambiguous")}
    field_counts = {name: {"valueChanged": 0, "sourceChanged": 0} for name in fields}
    report_hash = hashlib.sha256()
    byte_count = emitted = positions = 0
    offsets = []
    page_offsets = {kind: [] for kind in counts}
    page_counts = {kind: 0 for kind in counts}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="sf30-workbook-comparison-") as directory:
        os.chmod(directory, 0o700)
        db_path = os.path.join(directory, "join.sqlite")
        with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as db:
            os.chmod(db_path, 0o600)
            db.execute("PRAGMA temp_store=FILE")
            db.execute("PRAGMA cache_size=-16384")
            for table in ("baseline", "target"):
                db.execute("CREATE TABLE " + table + " (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY COLLATE BINARY, row_number INTEGER NOT NULL, record TEXT NOT NULL, tokens TEXT NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID")
            baseline = project(db, "baseline", 3, request["baseline"], keys, directory)
            db.commit()
            gc.collect()
            target = project(db, "target", 4, request["target"], keys, directory)
            db.commit()
            gc.collect()
            query = """SELECT b.key,b.record,b.tokens,t.record,t.tokens
                       FROM baseline b LEFT JOIN target t ON b.key=t.key
                       UNION ALL
                       SELECT t.key,NULL,NULL,t.record,t.tokens
                       FROM target t LEFT JOIN baseline b ON t.key=b.key WHERE b.key IS NULL
                       ORDER BY 1"""
            with os.fdopen(os.dup(5), "wb") as output:
                for key, old_raw, old_tokens, new_raw, new_tokens in db.execute(query):
                    old = json.loads(old_raw) if old_raw is not None else None
                    new = json.loads(new_raw) if new_raw is not None else None
                    old_values = json.loads(old_tokens) if old_tokens is not None else {}
                    new_values = json.loads(new_tokens) if new_tokens is not None else {}
                    moved = bool(old and new and old["row"] != new["row"])
                    if moved:
                        positions += 1
                    changes = []
                    for field in fields:
                        left_cell = old["cells"].get(field) if old else None
                        right_cell = new["cells"].get(field) if new else None
                        value_changed = old_values.get(field, ["missing", ""]) != new_values.get(field, ["missing", ""])
                        source_changed = cell_value(left_cell) != cell_value(right_cell)
                        if value_changed or source_changed:
                            field_counts[field]["valueChanged"] += int(value_changed)
                            field_counts[field]["sourceChanged"] += int(source_changed)
                            changes.append({
                                "field": field,
                                "before": old["values"].get(field) if old else None,
                                "after": new["values"].get(field) if new else None,
                                "beforeCell": left_cell.get("cell") if left_cell else None,
                                "afterCell": right_cell.get("cell") if right_cell else None,
                                "valueChanged": value_changed, "sourceChanged": source_changed})
                    if old is None:
                        kind = "added"
                    elif new is None:
                        kind = "removed"
                    elif any(x["valueChanged"] for x in changes):
                        kind = "changed"
                    elif changes:
                        kind = "source"
                    elif moved:
                        kind = "moved"
                    else:
                        kind = "unchanged"
                    counts[kind] += 1
                    visible = new if new is not None else old
                    specs = after_specs if new is not None else before_specs
                    row = {"ordinal": emitted, "kind": kind,
                           "key": [{"type": specs[name]["type"], "text": visible["values"][name]} for name in keys],
                           "before": old, "after": new, "changes": changes, "moved": moved}
                    raw = encoded(row) + b"\n"
                    if byte_count + len(raw) > maximum:
                        fail("WORKBOOK_COMPARISON_CAPACITY",
                             "The complete cell-change report exceeds its retained limit. Narrow the original range or increase the configured comparison limit.",
                             {"maxReportBytes": maximum, "rowsCompared": sum(counts.values())})
                    if emitted % 256 == 0:
                        offsets.append({"ordinal": emitted, "offset": byte_count})
                    views = [kind] + (["moved"] if moved and kind != "moved" else [])
                    for view in views:
                        logical = page_counts[view]
                        if logical % 256 == 0:
                            page_offsets[view].append({"logical": logical, "ordinal": emitted, "offset": byte_count})
                        page_counts[view] += 1
                    output.write(raw)
                    report_hash.update(raw)
                    byte_count += len(raw)
                    emitted += 1
                output.flush()
                os.fsync(output.fileno())
    return {"schema": "stellar-forge.workbook-edition-values.v1",
            "complete": True, "keys": keys, "columns": fields, "counts": counts,
            "positionsChanged": positions, "fieldCounts": field_counts,
            "rows": emitted, "rowBytes": byte_count, "rowsSha256": report_hash.hexdigest(),
            "rowOffsets": offsets, "pageOffsets": page_offsets,
            "baselineProjection": baseline, "targetProjection": target}

def main():
    if sys.version_info < (3, 10):
        raise RuntimeError("Python 3.10 or newer is required")
    request_raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read(2 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)
    if len(request_raw) > 2 * 1024 * 1024:
        raise ValueError("The comparison request exceeds 2 MiB")
    request = json.loads(request_raw)
    with os.fdopen(os.dup(6), "rb") as reader:
        reader.seek(0)
        reader_source = reader.read(256 * 1024 + 1)
    if len(reader_source) > 256 * 1024 or hashlib.sha256(reader_source).hexdigest() != request.get("parserSha256"):
        raise ValueError("The retained original reader does not match its identity")
    NATIVE["__name__"] = "stellar_forge_retained_workbook_reader"
    exec(compile(reader_source, "<retained-original-workbook-reader>", "exec"), NATIVE)
    csv.field_size_limit(NATIVE["LIMITS"]["cellChars"] * 2)
    if request.get("action") == "headers":
        return {"baseline": headers(3, request["baseline"]), "target": headers(4, request["target"])}
    if request.get("action") != "compare":
        fail("INVALID_WORKBOOK_ACTION", "Choose workbook headers or complete edition comparison.")
    return compare(request)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        result = main()
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(encoded({"ok": True, "result": result}) + b"\n")
    except Exception as error:
        known = hasattr(error, "code")
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(encoded({
            "ok": False, "error": error.code if known else "WORKBOOK_COMPARISON_FAILED",
            "message": str(error) if known else "The retained workbook comparison could not complete.",
            "details": getattr(error, "details", None)}) + b"\n")
        sys.exit(2)

# Use the merchant operator from a local MCP client

Connect an MCP host to the original Starforge merchant release operator as a
subprocess. The client receives the same twelve tools for source inspection,
staging, comparison, activation, seller startup, customer SDK export, rollback
and shutdown. The existing release store holds every version and selection;
the existing operator owns the seller it starts.

The subprocess uses the shared [MCP stdio transport](../mcp-paid-agent/stdio.mjs)
and starts the original [merchant factory](./serve.mjs) in one
[owned child](./merchant-host.mjs). Each request reaches the existing authenticated
HTTP handler through a private ephemeral loopback listener. The transport
generates its bearer internally and receives the child address through local IPC.
Standard output contains one complete JSON-RPC message per line. Both child
output streams go to standard error, including the original SF61 compiler's
direct stdout writes and trusted application diagnostics.

## Prepare the existing merchant

Use Node 22+ on the host that will run the merchant and keep the complete
installed Starforge source available. Follow the original
[merchant preparation guide](./README.md). For existing OpenAPI inputs:

```sh
node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/serve.mjs init \
  --dir /private/my-merchant \
  --spec /private/api/openapi.json \
  --selections /private/api/selections.json \
  --bindings /private/api/bindings.json \
  --name "My merchant" --seller-port 0
```

The resulting `merchant-mcp.json` fixes the private release store, customer
export directory, approved source aliases and runtime configuration. Existing
trusted handlers, upstream bindings and facilitator settings continue to use
the formats supported by the installed original merchant. MCP callers select
those aliases when preparing a release.

Keep backend credential values in the host's existing environment. The
registration below exports only the chosen merchant configuration path.

## Generate the host registration

Run this command on the machine that will launch the subprocess:

```sh
node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/client-config.mjs \
  --config /private/my-merchant/merchant-mcp.json \
  --name starforge-merchant \
  --output /private/starforge-merchant-host.json
```

The original merchant reader checks the selected configuration, release store
and export directory. The generator then creates a new private JSON file with
the actual absolute Node executable and installed entry path. Its shape is:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "starforge-merchant": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/node",
      "args": [
        "/absolute/path/to/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/stdio.mjs"
      ],
      "env": {
        "MCP_MERCHANT_CONFIG": "/private/my-merchant/merchant-mcp.json"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Use the generated paths with the MCP host's subprocess configuration. To
compose with an existing host file, add `--merge` and select a different output:

```sh
node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/client-config.mjs \
  --config /private/my-merchant/merchant-mcp.json \
  --name starforge-merchant \
  --merge /private/current-host.json \
  --output /private/combined-host.json
```

All existing settings and servers are retained. An existing registration with
the selected name is reported as a conflict; choose an unused name. New output
files use mode `0600`, and an existing output is preserved. Merged configurations
are written to the selected private file because they can contain the host's
other service credentials.

A host can also launch the entry directly:

```sh
node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/stdio.mjs \
  --config /private/my-merchant/merchant-mcp.json
```

Alternatively set the absolute path in `MCP_MERCHANT_CONFIG` and launch the entry
without arguments. The MCP host supplies standard input and reads standard
output. Prepare registration again after moving the installed source or Node
executable so the command resolves to their actual new paths.

## Complete the merchant workflow

The host initializes MCP, sends `notifications/initialized`, and lists tools.
Use the original tool schemas and returned values throughout the session:

1. Call `merchant_sources` for the configured alias, then `merchant_stage` with
   that alias and a new release ID. Inspect the exact digest and compare its
   routes and payment choices with the current selection.
2. Activate the reviewed release using its returned digest and current selection
   generation. Start that selection with `merchant_start`. Its returned operator
   instance ID identifies the seller owned by this subprocess.
3. Inspect actual seller metadata with `merchant_catalog`, and create a new
   named customer package with `merchant_client_export`. The package uses the
   original SDK exporter and original seller metadata.
4. Stage and review a later release, select it with the current generation, and
   restart the owned instance. Rollback selects an exact retained release through
   the same original history; restart applies that selection to the seller.
5. Call `merchant_stop`, or close the MCP subprocess. Closing waits for its
   accepted mutation and then drains the seller owned by that process.

The exact argument and result details remain in the
[original merchant tool guide](./README.md#complete-operator-workflow).

## Cancellation, reconnect and shutdown

An MCP cancellation stops this transport's wait for that request. A merchant
change already admitted by the original operator continues under its existing
release and instance tracking. Reconnect and inspect `merchant_status`, the
specific release and current generation before deciding how to continue an
interrupted stage, activation, export or restart. Completed release versions,
selection history and customer exports remain in the existing private store.

Closing standard input, a broken output stream, SIGINT or SIGTERM starts the
same graceful shutdown. The owned child finishes the original operator's
admitted change and drains its seller. Startup signals are retained while the
original factory opens so shutdown can complete as soon as that instance is
available. Parent IPC disconnection also drains the child; unexpected child exit
closes the MCP connection.

Each subprocess has its own initialization state and request IDs. Duplicate
active IDs are rejected. The shared transport handles UTF-8 across stream
chunks, output backpressure, cancellation and its configured concurrency limit.
The original merchant remains the authority for source aliases, generation
conflicts, instance ownership and release recovery.

## Embed and package

`startMerchantMcpStdio({configPath, environment, input, output, maxConcurrent,
diagnostic})` returns the shared transport's `close` function and `closed`
promise. The configuration path must be absolute. `durable` is true because the
original merchant release store is retained; readiness and the active release
are read through the original merchant tools.

`createMerchantMcpClientConfiguration({configPath, name, nodePath, entryPath,
existingConfiguration})` is the pure registration builder. The CLI adds the
original configuration-read check and private create-only output. Keep
`stdio.mjs`, `merchant-host.mjs`, `client-config.mjs` and this guide alongside the
original merchant component, plus the shared paid-agent stdio module and its
existing import closure. This is the same source layout used by the cumulative
distribution.

# Java customer SDK

Use the maintained Stellar Forge buyer from Java 17 or newer. The SDK provides
durable request creation, native review and execution, original-attempt recovery,
inbox operation, whole-object and paged-dataset acquisition, verified file
delivery and streaming record consumption.

The selected Node buyer remains the payment, approval, accounting and recovery
implementation. Java calls its existing bridge and reopens the same private
application state as the Node and Go customers.

## Build and select the installed runtime

Use a Java 17+ JDK and the Node/Python runtime required by the selected
[original buyer](../README.md). This SDK uses only the Java standard library.

From this directory, create the customer JAR in a new output directory:

~~~sh
java Build.java /absolute/new-java-build
java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar help
~~~

The builder compiles with Java release 17 and creates the command-line JAR.
It downloads no dependencies. Keep the JAR with the source revision you selected.
An application can add that JAR to its classpath:

~~~sh

For Gradle, the same local dependency is:

`runtimeDirectory` is the original SF88 directory containing `node/index.mjs`,
`go/bridge.mjs` and the native commands. An installed source edition includes it
under:

~~~
/absolute/application/node_modules/@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli
~~~

`stateDirectory` is the customer's private original Node application directory.
Choose absolute paths. Reuse that directory when reopening an existing
application. A distinct `.java-calls` directory holds Java invocation records;
the original intent and acquisition directories retain their existing format.

The private state and invocation directories use POSIX permissions. Run on the
same Linux/macOS/POSIX operator host as the native buyer, including an existing
WSL operator environment when appropriate. Select the actual installed Node
executable if it is outside the host's normal PATH.

~~~java
import io.starforge.buyer.Buyer;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Duration;

Buyer buyer = Buyer.builder(
        Path.of("/absolute/sf88-runtime"),
        Path.of("/absolute/private/java-customer"))
    .node("/absolute/node")
    .operatorProfile(Path.of("/absolute/private/operator-profile.json"))
    .approvalInput(true)
    .nativeTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(6))
    .cleanupGrace(Duration.ofSeconds(15))
    .build();

System.out.println(buyer.ready());
~~~

`build()` selects and inspects the original runtime files. `ready()` opens the
private application state through the maintained Node implementation.

The environment is inherited by default. Calling `environment(Map<String,
String>)` selects a complete replacement environment for the child, including
any PATH and existing provider references it needs. Credential values stay in
that process environment.

## Create, review, execute and reopen

`Buyer.create` accepts the original saved buyer configuration or a Java JSON
object. `Buyer.request` accepts the native request fields. `importOperation`
accepts the merchant's original portable handoff and an explicit payment-option
index. `prepare` retains the selected catalog row, request and payment option.

~~~java
import io.starforge.buyer.Json;
import io.starforge.buyer.Operation;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.Map;

Operation operation = buyer.create(
    Path.of("/absolute/private/buyer-request.json"),
    new Buyer.CreateOptions());

Map<String, Object> review = operation.review();
System.out.println(Json.stringify(review));
Operation.Result result = operation.execute(review);

System.out.println(result.status());
if (result.ok()) {
    Object response = operation.file().json(8 * 1024 * 1024);
    System.out.println(Json.stringify(response));
}
~~~

Configure the original operator profile before creating the request. Creation
retains the request, profile, exact body, response settings and any operation
ticket. The review passed to `execute` belongs to that same retained operation.
The original native terminal and spending policy then operate on the current
merchant challenge.

An intent ID is durable. After reopening the application:

~~~java
Operation original = buyer.operation("report-2026-10");
Operation.State state = original.inspect();
var completed = original.recover();
if (completed.isPresent()) {
    System.out.println(completed.get().status());
}
~~~

An empty recovery result means the original attempt has no complete recoverable
result yet. The same `inspect`, native logs and original recovery workflow show
its current state. An existing attempt continues under its same identity.

`CreateOptions.body(null)` leaves the body absent. `body(new byte[0])` preserves
an explicitly empty body. Provided bytes travel as base64 in the private call
file. An original configuration's `operation.bodyFile` continues through the
native request-file reader.

`responseFile` accepts the original response limits, expected type/digest and
stream options; the Node application owns its destination. `requestTimeout`
sets the native merchant HTTP deadline, from 1 to 300000 milliseconds.

~~~java
Buyer.CreateOptions options = new Buyer.CreateOptions()
    .body(requestBytes)
    .requestTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(120))
    .responseFile(Json.map("maxBytes", 64 * 1024 * 1024, "timeoutMs", 120000));

Operation operation = buyer.request(Json.map(
    "intentId", "report-2026-10",
    "url", originalMerchantUrl,
    "method", "POST",
    "expect", originalExpectedTerms,
    "headers", originalRequestHeaders
), options);
~~~

The corresponding command-line workflow uses the same Java SDK:

~~~sh
java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar \
  --runtime /absolute/sf88-runtime --state /absolute/private/java-customer \
  --profile /absolute/private/operator-profile.json \
  create --config /absolute/private/buyer-request.json

java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar \
  --runtime /absolute/sf88-runtime --state /absolute/private/java-customer \
  review --id report-2026-10 --save-result /absolute/private/original-review.json

java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar \
  --runtime /absolute/sf88-runtime --state /absolute/private/java-customer \
  --approval-input execute --id report-2026-10 \
  --review /absolute/private/original-review.json

java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar \
  --runtime /absolute/sf88-runtime --state /absolute/private/java-customer \
  recover --id report-2026-10
~~~

`--approval-input` inherits the caller's real stdin. The Java SDK never supplies
an approval answer. Interactive customers should serialize use of one terminal.
The native approval implementation retains its own terminal requirements.

## Consume verified bytes and records

`operation.file()` addresses its original saved response. `NativeFile` also
addresses an inbox response, an assembled object, a dataset export or a retained
native `BuyerResult`.

| Method | Customer use |
| --- | --- |
| `verify()` | Read the original checked byte count and digest. |
| `saveAs(Path)` | Create a verified copy through the original synchronized file publisher. |
| `writeTo(OutputStream)` | Stream a complete response with bounded Java buffering. |
| `bytes(int)` | Read a complete response within an explicit memory limit. |
| `json(int)` | Decode verified UTF-8 JSON using exact decimal Java numbers. |
| `records(Format, Map, RecordConsumer)` | Consume the original NDJSON, SSE, CSV or typed dataset decoder. |

`bytes` accepts zero to 256 MiB. Use `writeTo` for larger resources. A zero limit
can receive a zero-byte file. The returned transfer records the original byte
count and digest.

~~~java
var info = buyer.operation("report-2026-10").file()
    .saveAs(Path.of("/absolute/private/report.json"));
System.out.println(info.bytes());
System.out.println(info.sha256());
~~~

A streaming callback receives data before the original decoder completes its
final checks. Commit downstream effects after the method returns successfully.
A callback can throw `IOException` to stop the original transfer.

~~~java
import io.starforge.buyer.NativeFile;

NativeFile.Transfer transfer = buyer.operation("market-events").file().records(
    NativeFile.Format.SSE,
    Json.map("allowPartial", true),
    event -> System.out.println(Json.stringify(event)));

System.out.println(transfer.records());
~~~

`allowPartial` selects the original decoder's complete-record prefix of a partial
native capture. Original stream metadata and framing rules remain attached.
CSV options include the existing `headers`, `maxFieldCharacters` and
`maxRowCharacters` fields. Dataset records use the original typed row decoder.

The Java bridge-record limit defaults to 16 MiB per encoded record. Its explicit
overload supports up to 256 MiB, independently of the native decoder limits.

~~~sh
java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar \
  --runtime /absolute/sf88-runtime --state /absolute/private/java-customer \
  file-copy --id report-2026-10 --out /absolute/private/report-copy.json

java -jar /absolute/new-java-build/starforge-buyer.jar \
  --runtime /absolute/sf88-runtime --state /absolute/private/java-customer \
  file-records --id market-events --format sse --partial
~~~

`file-read` writes exact streamed bytes to stdout. `file-records` writes one JSON
value per line. Their original transfer metadata goes to stderr. `file-json`
produces a structured JSON value and accepts `--limit`.
